{"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1794713222509,"sessionID":"ses_e22c8f413ffe31f3hJL31TFhpX","part":{"id":"prt_1dd3e1ac8001pZOp2nSP31ERPW","messageID":"msg_1dd3d4726001lLdlAQ2Jjkqocf","sessionID":"ses_e22c8f413ffe31f3hJL31TFhpX","type":"reasoning","text":"**Discovering Relevant Data**\n\nI've hit the motherlode on day two! This is an exciting starting point, and I'm very happy with this finding!\n\n\n**Unmasking the Decoy**\n\nI've made a crucial breakthrough! The access logs for `e37` on Day 1 are highly suspicious, especially considering the unhappy message. Those three after-hours accesses on day 1 seem like a deliberate attempt at misdirection. Further analysis of the total log entries on Day 1 (48 entries across 40 employees) indicates that this is a genuine log, not a test.\n\n\n**Analyzing After-Hours Patterns**\n\nI'm now diving deep into those after-hours entries on Day 1. The Poisson distribution is helping to frame expected access numbers. The discrepancy between the expected (42) and actual (48) entries is interesting. Those specific `after_hours: true` entries are jumping out at me, especially `e37`'s triple appearance. I must check messages from day 1 for confirmation!\n\n\n**Identifying Potential Candidates**\n\nI've shifted focus to identifying the true targets within Engineering and Research. Since `e37` is almost certainly a decoy, I need to know how many non-decoy employees remain.  There are 5 in Engineering (excluding `e37`) and 5 in Research, totaling 10 potential candidates. The original plan in `c2-1` now needs recalculation!\n\n\n**Evaluating Day 2 Data**\n\nI'm now zeroing in on Day 2's regular documents and their recipients. A striking pattern has emerged: Engineering, with its six members, received zero regular documents on that day. Legal, with seven, also received none! This is a major clue that I'm keen to exploit. This is a game changer, the new Canary plan is now to target Engineering and Legal departments!\n\n\n**Confirming Leaking Document**\n\nI've just confirmed the smoking gun. If the mole is in Engineering and has a \"newest\" DSL rule, document `c2-1` is the only age-zero document on Day 2, and the mole leaks it with certainty. Even under random distribution, `c2-1`'s high weight and smaller size (10) for few_recipients, strongly implicates it. Planting `c2-1` alone on Day 2 looks like the ideal, cost-effective canary strategy! This seems like a slam dunk now.\n\n\n**Refining Target Demographics**\n\nI'm revisiting the potential target pool, specifically considering the Day 3 leak window. The key question is whether to re-include `e37` in the mix, and I need to calculate it properly. I've re-analyzed the probability of `e37` being a decoy: the angry message and after-hours accesses give an incredibly high probability. Therefore, I can exclude `e37` and I can proceed with the target group of size ten.\n\n\n**Optimizing Canary Deployment**\n\nI've just devised a highly effective canary deployment strategy. Assigning `c2-1` to variants `\"A\"`, `\"B\"`, and `\"C\"` with specific Engineering and Research employee distributions makes the plan. If `c2-1` leaks alongside a department-separating document, we'll narrow down the suspects to a handful. Furthermore, I have five actions to perform further interviews on Day 2 to finalize the investigation!\n\n\n","time":{"start":1794713197256,"end":1794713222489}}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1794713706548,"sessionID":"ses_e22c8f413ffe31f3hJL31TFhpX","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"qzAGM5UaXMw2GvDy","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"content":"import math\n\n# All 9 surviving candidates (intersection of c1-2 and d1-2)\ncandidates = {\n    \"e21\": {\"dept\": \"Legal\", \"c1_2\": \"B\"},\n    \"e32\": {\"dept\": \"Sales\", \"c1_2\": \"B\"},\n    \"e39\": {\"dept\": \"Sales\", \"c1_2\": \"B\"},\n    \"e17\": {\"dept\": \"Legal\", \"c1_2\": \"A\"},\n    \"e24\": {\"dept\": \"Sales\", \"c1_2\": \"A\"},\n    \"e27\": {\"dept\": \"Sales\", \"c1_2\": \"A\"},\n    \"e30\": {\"dept\": \"Legal\", \"c1_2\": \"C\"},\n    \"e33\": {\"dept\": \"Sales\", \"c1_2\": \"C\"},\n    \"e34\": {\"dept\": \"Sales\", \"c1_2\": \"C\"},\n}\n\nlogs = [\n    # Day 1\n    (\"e03\", False), (\"e03\", False), (\"e16\", False), (\"e16\", False), (\"e17\", False),\n    (\"e24\", False), (\"e27\", False), (\"e27\", False), (\"e27\", False), (\"e30\", False),\n    (\"e30\", False), (\"e30\", False), (\"e32\", False), (\"e32\", False), (\"e33\", False),\n    (\"e33\", True), (\"e34\", False), (\"e34\", False),\n    # Day 2\n    (\"e17\", False), (\"e21\", False), (\"e30\", False), (\"e32\", False), (\"e34\", False),\n    # Day 3\n    (\"e17\", False), (\"e17\", True), (\"e24\", False), (\"e24\", False), (\"e27\", False),\n    (\"e27\", False), (\"e30\", False), (\"e30\", False), (\"e30\", False), (\"e32\", False),\n    (\"e34\", False), (\"e34\", True), (\"e34\", False),\n    # Day 4\n    (\"e21\", False), (\"e21\", False), (\"e24\", False), (\"e24\", False), (\"e30\", True),\n    (\"e33\", False), (\"e33\", False), (\"e34\", False),\n]\n\n# Interviews: (emp, evasive_bool)\ninterviews = [\n    (\"e33\", True),   # Day 2 recent_documents\n    (\"e21\", False),  # Day 3 recent_documents\n    (\"e39\", True),   # Day 4 recent_documents\n    (\"e32\", False),  # Day 4 recent_documents\n    (\"e21\", True),   # Day 4 contacts_outside\n]\n\n# Compute log-likelihoods (assuming default random mole for doc choice, plus separate check without doc-count factor)\nfor mode in [\"pure_canary_logs_interviews\", \"with_default_random_d1_2\"]:\n    weights = {}\n    for emp, info in candidates.items():\n        w = 0.95 if info[\"c1_2\"] == \"B\" else 0.025\n        ah_true = sum(1 for e, ah in logs if e == emp and ah)\n        ah_false = sum(1 for e, ah in logs if e == emp and not ah)\n        # Mole: ah_true ~ Pois(0.3), ah_false ~ Pois(0.7)\n        # Innocent non-decoy: ah_true ~ Pois(0.1 + 1/38), ah_false ~ Pois(0.9)\n        lr_ah_true = 0.3 / (0.1 + 1.0 / 38.0)\n        lr_ah_false = 0.7 / 0.9\n        w *= (lr_ah_true ** ah_true) * (lr_ah_false ** ah_false)\n        for e, ev in interviews:\n            if e == emp:\n                w *= 1.2 if ev else (0.76 / 0.80)\n        if mode == \"with_default_random_d1_2\":\n            # Under default random mole:\n            # Legal on Day 2 only held d1-2 -> leaks d1-2 w.p. 0.65 (delay 3 -> Day 5 w.p. 0.5) = 0.325\n            # Or didn't leak Day 2 (0.35) and on Day 3 held d1-2, d3-1, (and c3, c3-2 for B):\n            if info[\"dept\"] == \"Legal\":\n                if info[\"c1_2\"] == \"B\":\n                    p_d1_2_surf5 = 0.65 * 0.5 + 0.35 * 0.65 * (1.0 / (2.0 + 1.75)) * 0.5\n                else:\n                    p_d1_2_surf5 = 0.65 * 0.5 + 0.35 * 0.65 * (1.0 / 2.0) * 0.5\n            else:\n                # Sales on Day 2 held d1-2, d2-2, d2-3 (3 docs): leaks d1-2 w.p. 0.65*(1/3), surf5 w.p. 0.5\n                # Or didn't leak d1-2 on Day 2 (1 - 0.65/3), and on Day 3 held remaining (avg ~3.35 reg docs + canaries)\n                if info[\"c1_2\"] == \"B\":\n                    p_d1_2_surf5 = 0.65 * (1/3) * 0.5 + (1 - 0.65/3) * 0.65 * (1.0 / (3.5 + 1.75)) * 0.5\n                else:\n                    p_d1_2_surf5 = 0.65 * (1/3) * 0.5 + (1 - 0.65/3) * 0.65 * (1.0 / 3.5) * 0.5\n            w *= p_d1_2_surf5\n        weights[emp] = w\n\n    tot = sum(weights.values())\n    print(f\"=== {mode} ===\")\n    for emp, w in sorted(weights.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):\n        ah_t = sum(1 for e, ah in logs if e == emp and ah)\n        ah_f = sum(1 for e, ah in logs if e == emp and not ah)\n        print(f\"  {emp} ({candidates[emp]['dept']}, c1-2={candidates[emp]['c1_2']}, ah={ah_t}/{ah_t+ah_f}): {w/tot:.4%}\")\n","filePath":"/tmp/opencode/bayes.py"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/tmp/opencode/bayes.py","exists":false,"truncated":false},"title":"tmp/opencode/bayes.py","time":{"start":1794713706514,"end":1794713706536}},"metadata":{"google":{"thoughtSignature":""}},"id":"prt_1dd45dfe5001RIL1AmOVnrNCEK","sessionID":"ses_e22c8f413ffe31f3hJL31TFhpX","messageID":"msg_1dd4546280017Izd0nyMoo7J1H"}}

{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1794714220129,"sessionID":"ses_e22c8f413ffe31f3hJL31TFhpX","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"mKuT380RYMQkwmq4","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/tmp/opencode/final_check.py","content":"# Exact data copied from server JSON responses\nc1_2_variants = {\"A\": [\"e09\", \"e17\", \"e22\", \"e24\", \"e27\"], \"B\": [\"e11\", \"e21\", \"e32\", \"e36\", \"e39\"], \"C\": [\"e18\", \"e30\", \"e33\", \"e34\"]}\nd1_2_recipients = set([\"e02\", \"e03\", \"e08\", \"e10\", \"e12\", \"e13\", \"e16\", \"e17\", \"e21\", \"e24\", \"e27\", \"e28\", \"e29\", \"e30\", \"e32\", \"e33\", \"e34\", \"e38\", \"e39\"])\nc3_variants = {\"A\": [\"e11\", \"e32\"], \"C\": [\"e21\"], \"B\": [\"e36\", \"e39\"]}\nc4_variants = {\"A\": [\"e11\"], \"B\": [\"e21\", \"e39\"], \"C\": [\"e32\", \"e36\"]}\n\nc1_2_rec = set(sum(c1_2_variants.values(), []))\nc3_rec = set(sum(c3_variants.values(), []))\nc4_rec = set(sum(c4_variants.values(), []))\n\ninter = c1_2_rec & d1_2_recipients & c3_rec & c4_rec\nprint(\"Exact intersection of all 4 leaked docs:\", sorted(inter))\n\n# Check variants for each survivor:\n# Leaked: c1-2 -> B, c3 -> C, c4 -> B\nweights = {}\nfor emp in sorted(inter):\n    w = 1.0\n    for vmap, leaked_v in [(c1_2_variants, \"B\"), (c3_variants, \"C\"), (c4_variants, \"B\")]:\n        n_other = len(vmap) - 1\n        if emp in vmap[leaked_v]:\n            w *= 0.95\n        else:\n            w *= 0.05 / n_other\n    weights[emp] = w\n\n# Add access logs Days 1-6 for e21, e32, e39:\n# e21: D1:0, D2:1F, D3:0, D4:2F, D5:1F, D6:1T -> 1T, 4F\n# e32: D1:2F, D2:1F, D3:1F, D4:0, D5:2F, D6:3F+1T -> 1T, 9F\n# e39: D1:0, D2:0, D3:0, D4:0, D5:1F, D6:2F -> 0T, 3F\nlogs_counts = {\"e21\": (1, 4), \"e32\": (1, 9), \"e39\": (0, 3)}\n# Interviews Days 1-6:\n# e21: D3:F, D4:T, D5:F,F, D6:F -> 1 evasive, 4 coop\n# e32: D4:F, D5:F,F, D6:F -> 0 evasive, 4 coop\n# e39: D4:T, D5:F,F, D6:T -> 2 evasive, 2 coop\nint_counts = {\"e21\": (1, 4), \"e32\": (0, 4), \"e39\": (2, 2)}\n\nlr_t = 0.3 / (0.1 + 1/38)\nlr_f = 0.7 / 0.9\nfor emp in weights:\n    t, f = logs_counts[emp]\n    ev, coop = int_counts[emp]\n    weights[emp] *= (lr_t ** t) * (lr_f ** f) * (1.2 ** ev) * ((0.76/0.80) ** coop)\n\ntot = sum(weights.values())\nfor emp, w in sorted(weights.items(), key=lambda x: -x[1]):\n    print(f\"{emp}: {w/tot:.6%}\")\n"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/tmp/opencode/final_check.py","exists":false,"truncated":false},"title":"tmp/opencode/final_check.py","time":{"start":1794714220113,"end":1794714220125}},"metadata":{"google":{"thoughtSignature":""}},"id":"prt_1dd4db62d001zqOYSrZgYN1GIK","sessionID":"ses_e22c8f413ffe31f3hJL31TFhpX","messageID":"msg_1dd4b52190015K8YZpbLSOHDOd"}}
